dice.$comment: Same notation as a Strike's damage.

when.$comment: Which level the number is counted from: the base creature's ('starting level', the tables Elite, Weak, Vampire, Werecreature print) or the new creature's (default).

tier.$comment: A tier of a creature-building scale — the value the scale record row carries for the creature's level. `unlimited | limited` are the Area Damage table's columns ('limited use area damage for a creature of the graveknight's level').
One tier, or a pair of alternatives printed as 'a moderate or high' that the user picks between. Only tiers the scale record carries are valid — the validator checks the reference.

part.$comment: Which number of a two-number cell the reference reads: the Spell DC table prints a DC and a spell attack modifier in each cell. Required on a reference into such a scale and absent otherwise — the validator's rule.

delta.$comment: A shift printed on top of the scale value: 'spell DC – 2'.

byLevel.$comment: A value that holds from its level upward ('increases to 10 at 9th level and 15 at 16th'); levels strictly increasing is the validator's rule.

ofLevel.$comment: A fraction of the creature's level: 0.5 for 'half its level'.

round.$comment: How a fractional level is rounded; without it, the game's own rule.

min.$comment: The printed floor: an integer beside `ofLevel` ('one-third its level (minimum 1)'), a die expression beside `dice` ('1d6 per 2 levels (minimum 1d6)').

dice.$comment: The part that repeats with level: '1d6 plus 1d6 for every 2 levels' holds dice '1d6' per 2 levels.

base.$comment: The flat part printed before the repeating one.

levelValue.$comment: A number a template prints that depends on the creature's level: never only prose.

modifyStat.$comment: What a `modify` shifts. `saves` shifts all three saving throws; `fortitude`/`reflex`/`will` name one when the template does.

limited.$comment: The smaller shift the template prints for an ability with a limit on its frequency.

value.$comment: An integer, or a level-dependent one: the ghost's all-damage resistance, the vampire's fast healing.

except.$comment: Same vocabulary as the creature's own `except`.

typed.$comment: An entry of `resistances` or `weaknesses`, as the creature's typed one, with a `value` a template may express per level.

attributes.$comment: A replacement of the base creature's attribute modifiers, printed in full ('a ghost has a Strength modifier of –5 and a Constitution modifier of +0'). The template names only the attributes it replaces; the rest are the base creature's.

traitsOp.$comment: Traits added to or dropped from the base creature. The sentence that qualifies them ('many become unholy') stays in `caveats`.

remove.$comment: Abilities the base creature loses, by their ids within the creature. The validator checks each creature listed in `appliesTo.creatures` actually has them.

items.$comment: The text of the base creature's ability is swapped for the printed one ('the Sinful Bite effect of the sin'). `from` is by id within the creature; the validator checks it is there.

byCreature.$comment: Spell blocks keyed by the creature they belong to: a dragon age's expanded list, with every rank spelled out even where the book prints 'as young …, plus …'.

speeds.$comment: A speed replaced: feet, or equal to one of the creature's own speeds the book prints ('fly Speed equal to its Speed').

stats.$comment: The numbers rebuilt to the creature's new level: each keeps its printed tier and takes its value from that tier's cell in the scale record at the new level. The rule that finds the tier — nearest cell, a range as its midpoint, ties up — is stated in the dataset README. Strikes: the attack bonus by scale.strike-attack, the damage by scale.strike-damage. HP: the tier's range midpoint, rounded down.

keep.$comment: 'Do not modify the Hit Points due to its new level.'

delta.$comment: A shift, or the per-level table the template prints ('by the amount listed on the table'), expressed per level.

oneOf.$comment: The book prints a range to pick from ('increase the level by 6 to 10').

name.$comment: The printed name of the curse or disease, when the ability names it apart from its own.

dc.$comment: An integer, or a level-dependent DC: 'the high spell DC of the creature's level'.

affliction.$comment: A curse or disease the added ability inflicts, in the shape a hazard ability's effect carries.

id.$comment: Unique within the adjustment; what a Strike effect points at with `own`.

ability.$comment: The universal ability this entry is an instance of (Darkvision, Fast Healing, Stench). The validator checks the record exists.

values.$comment: The level-dependent numbers of the ability, by a stable slug: `amount` for Fast Healing's value, `damage` for a repeating die. The printed text keeps its prose; the engine computes from here.

ability.$comment: An added or replacement ability, in the shape of a creature's ability plus the level-dependent `values` and an `affliction` the ability inflicts.

material.$comment: The precious material the Strike counts as; silver for a Curse of the Werecreature's delivered curse.

effects.$comment: A universal ability by its record, or text the book prints for the hit.

derive.$comment: The printed rule that stands where damage dice would ('roughly the same as the damage dealt by its other attacks'). The game shows it; the engine computes no number from it.

strike.$comment: A Strike a template prints. Each field is what the book actually prints — some templates print no dice at all and give the rule in `derive` — so unlike a creature's Strike every field is optional.

max.$comment: How many entries the player picks at least; a `min` of 0 is the template's 'optional'.

items.$comment: From this level of the new creature up, the choice widens or narrows: from 9th, a ghost picks as many as three.

id.$comment: Unique within the adjustment; what a Strike effect points at with `own`.

entry.$comment: One choice of an ability option: the ability itself plus any operations it brings (Unkillable raises the level by 1, a sin swaps Sinful Bite). Not composed of `ability` and the operation fields by `allOf` — a referenced `additionalProperties: false` would reject the sibling fields — so its shape is spelled out here; keep it in step with those defs.

substituteFor.$comment: An Alternate-abilities list: each entry replaces one of the base creature's printed abilities, by id (the Lich's frightful presence). The validator checks each creature in `appliesTo.creatures` has them.

living.$comment: 'turn living creatures into…': the base creature's nature the template states, expressed by what the print says.

family.$comment: Only members of the printed family are affected (a Skeleton Abilities set).

creatures.$comment: Only these creatures (Greater Herexen over creature.herexen).

traits.$comment: The creature must carry all these traits (a living humanoid, for Werecreature).

spellcaster.$comment: Only a creature with a spell block (the Lich).

requires.$comment: Applied only on top of another adjustment first (True Vampire over Vampire).

note.$comment: A condition the fields above cannot express, as printed.

family.$comment: The family whose page prints the transformation. Elite and Weak have none.

delta.$comment: Steps on the size scale: +1 one category up, −1 down.

traitsOp.$comment: Traits added to or dropped from the base creature, spelled out apart from the record's envelope `traits` — those are the adjustment's own (usually empty). Renamed here because the envelope already owns the name `traits` at the record's root.

caveats.$comment: Every printed sentence the operations above cannot express — in the order the page prints it. The engine shows them to the player or the GM.
